title: The Night Court
description: A reign of ten years, then one night in the hall told minute by minute.
premise: Queen Maret's oath opens a long reign. Years later, one night at Harthall puts Lord Calder in two quarrels at once.
tone: Cold stone, candle smoke, a clock that matters
themes: What a court remembers, and what it cannot date
writing_style: Close third, plain verbs, time stated exactly

entities.name: Queen Maret
entities.notes: Crowned at the new year 1000. She keeps the hall's clock herself.

entities.name: Lord Calder
entities.notes: Holds a grudge he will not date, and attends the night anyway.

entities.name: Harthall
entities.notes: The queen's hall. One night here is told in minutes; the reign before it, in years.

events.title: The old grudge
events.description: A quarrel Calder says ended the summer before the oath, and will not say when it began.

events.title: Since the grudge
events.description: He dates his slight to the start of that quarrel. The start was never written down.

events.title: The oath
events.description: Maret swears the oath at the new year.

events.title: The coronation
events.description: The crown follows the oath, at the oath's end.

events.title: The first decree
events.description: The first decree is read as the coronation begins, and the coronation is the oath's end.

events.title: The reign
events.description: Ten years from the oath's end to midsummer 1010.

events.title: A name forgotten
events.description: A guest the lists leave out.

events.title: The lost hour
events.description: A bell the court remembers and cannot date, because the guest it marked has no time.

events.title: The snow
events.description: Snow begins in the afternoon. No one records when it stops.

events.title: Before the feast
events.description: The hall is quiet from noon until the feast begins.

events.title: The feast
events.description: The feast fills the hall from six until eleven.

events.title: Seated
events.description: The queen sits as the feast starts.

events.title: The announcement
events.description: Her announcement is the moment she sits, which is the moment the feast starts.

events.title: The ride
events.description: Calder rides in at half past six and is in the hall until the toast begins.

events.title: The dance
events.description: The dance runs inside the feast, from seven until half past nine.

events.title: The argument
events.description: From eight until ten Calder argues with the queen, overlapping the dance and still inside the feast.

events.title: The toast
events.description: The toast is raised at nine.

events.title: The bell
events.description: The hall bell strikes nine, the same moment as the toast.

events.title: The three knocks
events.description: Three knocks, minutes apart. Nothing is continuous between them.

events.title: Between the knocks
events.description: A telling that treats the knocks as one moment. They are three, so it does not resolve.

events.title: The last cup
events.description: The last cup is the feast's end.

events.title: After the feast
events.description: The hall stays lit from the feast's end until one.

events.title: The rumor
events.description: Something happened in the hall. No one agrees when, or that it had a start or an end.

events.title: The contradiction
events.description: A garbled telling that puts the toast before the oath.

arcs.title: The old claim
arcs.description: From the oath to the toast, and a guest with no time.

arcs.title: The night
arcs.description: The feast, the ride, the dance, the argument, and the toast, in the order they start.

arcs.title: Told backwards
arcs.description: The argument, then the dance, then the feast: the night told against the order it happened.
